audit_findings.title: Finance-leased fleet additions may bypass the OE capital-expenditure deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $167m of filed 2025 noncash finance-lease additions; if wholly omitted and recurring, computed value overstatement is approximately $28.37/$37.46/$41.82 per share in bear/base/bull
audit_findings.mechanism: Noncash fleet additions can increase productive assets and depreciation without entering cash capital expenditures deducted from OE, overstating the OE anchor and every scenario derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Our finance lease obligations consist primarily of rental equipment (primarily vehicles) and building leases.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $167m of finance-leased additions, equal to 8.6% of the $1,951.1m anchor. The supplied record does not establish whether the OE calculation captured them, so omission is unresolved rather than demonstrated. The amount is large enough to affect valuation materially, although correcting it alone would not close the gap to the $1,008.03 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE capital-expenditure deduction to cash purchases, accounts-payable additions and finance-lease additions; then rerun all scenarios with finance-lease investment and related interest treatment applied consistently.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may capitalize acquisition growth without its recurring acquisition cost
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed acquisition spending was $357m in FY2025 and $400m in H1 2026; acquisition spending required for the 3%-5% forecasts is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings enter the historical OE base and forecast growth, while business-purchase cash flows sit outside ordinary capital expenditures and may therefore be omitted from OE reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: We have historically achieved a significant portion of our growth through acquisitions and we will continue to consider potential acquisitions on a selective basis.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate that the forecast growth cases depend on acquisitions, so this is an unresolved possibility. However, FY2025 acquisition spending alone was 18.3% of anchor OE, and H1 2026 spending was already $400m. That scale makes costless capitalization of acquisition-dependent growth reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Produce an organic revenue, OE and fleet-growth bridge excluding acquisitions; demonstrate that each growth case is organically financeable, or rerun the affected cases after deducting the acquisition investment required to achieve them.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 cash-tax benefit may not be a normalized perpetual cash flow
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed cash taxes fell from $994m in 2024 to $602m in 2025, a $392m decrease, while deferred taxes increased $405m; H1 2026 cash taxes were $158m versus $540m in H1 2025; normalized adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Lower current tax payments raise cash-based OE, while the offset accumulates in deferred-tax liabilities and may reverse when tax depreciation falls below book depreciation or fleet investment contracts.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon enactment in the third quarter of 2025, the legislation (i) did not materially impact our effective tax rate, (ii) decreased our cash income tax liability and (iii) increased our deferred tax liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate a large cash-tax reduction and increasing deferred taxes, but do not separate permanent savings from timing deferrals. The 2025 cash-tax decrease equals 20.1% of anchor OE, so perpetuating a material timing benefit could materially overstate value, especially in the shrinking-fleet bear case.
audit_findings.action: Build a book-to-cash tax schedule by scenario showing bonus depreciation, capital expenditures, deferred-tax additions and reversals; normalize the anchor and rerun the explicit and terminal periods using scenario-consistent cash taxes.

audit_findings.title: The anchor retains a nonrecurring merger-termination benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed benefit was $52m in operating cash flow/free cash flow and $29m after tax; capitalizing the full $52m produces a computed overstatement of approximately $8.84/$11.67/$13.03 per share in bear/base/bull
audit_findings.mechanism: The transaction-specific cash benefit raises the sole FY2025 OE anchor and is then capitalized through every forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, the impact of the merger termination was a $29 after-tax benefit, or $0.45 per diluted share, for net income and a $52 benefit for adjusted EBITDA (as defined below).
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that FY2025 operating cash flow and free cash flow included the $52m benefit. Even assuming the entire $52m remains in OE, it is only 2.7% of the anchor; removing it leaves the bull value near $477.48 per share, still far below the $1,008.03 market price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $64m fee and related professional and bridge-financing costs on a consistent cash-tax basis, document whether the anchor adjustment is $52m or $29m, and rerun the scenarios for accuracy.

audit_findings.title: An unquantified multiemployer-pension claim could rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: A withdrawal liability would be an additional senior claim against equity that is neither an ordinary annual OE expense nor included in the stated bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, a contributing employer to an underfunded multiemployer plan is liable, generally upon withdrawal from a plan, for its proportionate share of the plan's unfunded vested liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies a contingent withdrawal-liability mechanism but states that URI currently has no intention of withdrawing. No funded-status or company-specific exposure is supplied, so no present liability or demonstrated valuation error can be established. It is a forward-looking contingency to monitor rather than a presently quantified adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain plan-level funded status, URI contribution shares, estimated withdrawal liabilities, any recognized accruals and evidence of likely withdrawal or plan insolvency; add a bridge deduction and rerun only if a probable or reasonably estimable exposure emerges.

audit_findings.title: Known 2026 restructuring cash costs are absent from the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed expected total program charges are $55m-$65m; $50m was recognized and $24m paid through June 2026, with a $26m reserve; even an undiscounted $65m equity reduction is approximately $1.04 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: One-time restructuring cash payments affect near-term OE or the equity bridge but should not be capitalized as a perpetual reduction to normalized OE; any associated savings affect forecast growth and margins.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to complete this program in 2026, and expect to recognize between $ 30 and $ 60 of total costs, primarily comprised of severance and branch closure costs, under the program.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves much of the uncertainty: $50m had been recognized by June 2026, including noncash right-of-use asset impairments, and only $5m-$15m of additional charges were expected. The latest $112m cash bridge already reflects payments made through June. Even treating the full $65m program as an incremental equity outflow would equal only 0.24% of the $27,525m base equity value and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify remaining cash payments separately from noncash impairments, deduct any post-June cash obligation once in the near-term projection or bridge, and verify that forecast savings are included only if the necessary restructuring expenditures are also included.
